answer: The most convincing sybil defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers who countersign invalid transactions, priced above any epoch reward. In the Oasis network, each validation committee is a small reef of sampled nodes; an attacker must stake many identities to be sampled, but each marble of stake backing a fraudulent countersignature is burned on-chain. Since the slash exceeds a full epoch's rewards, a sybil operator loses more per attack than it can earn, making fake identities economically self-defeating.
